verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु। रुरुश्चुक्रोश गहनं वनं गत्वाऽतिदुःखितः॥१॥
verses.english: Sauti replied : While the noble Brahmanas were sitting round the dead body, Ruru, much aggrieved, retired into a deep forest and wept aloud.

verses.sanskrit: शोकेनाभिहतः सोऽथ विलपन्करुणं बहु। अब्रवीद्वचनं शोचन्प्रियां स्मृत्वा प्रमद्वराम्॥२॥
verses.english: Overwhelmed with grief, he indulged in much piteous lamentations. Remembering his beloved Pramadvara, he thus lamented in grief,
verses.bhavadeepa: नवमः अध्यायः  महामहिम्नाप्यायुषः क्षणोऽपि दुर्लभ इत्यर्थमध्याय आरभ्यते तेषु तत्रेत्यादिः ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: शेते सा भुवि तन्वङ्गी मम शोकविवर्धिनी। बान्धवानां च सर्वेषां किं नु दुःखमतःपरम्॥३॥
verses.english: “Alas! The slender-bodied beauty who increases my grief, is now lying on the bare ground. What can be more painful than this to all her friends!

verses.sanskrit: यदि दत्तं तपस्तप्तं गुरवो वा मया यदि। सम्यगाराधितास्तेन संजीवतु मम प्रिया॥४॥
verses.english: If ever I have bestowed charity, if ever I have observed penances, if ever I have showed respect to my superiors, let the merits of these acts restore to life my beloved one.

verses.sanskrit: यथा च जन्मप्रभृति यतात्माऽहं धृतव्रतः। प्रमद्वरा तथा ह्येषा समुत्तिष्ठतु भामिनी॥५॥
verses.english: If ever I have controlled my passions from my birth, if ever I have stuck to my vows, let the beautiful Pramadvara rise from the ground.”

verses.sanskrit: एवं लालप्यतस्तस्य भार्यार्थे दुःखितस्य च। देवदूतस्तदाऽभ्येत्य वाक्यमाह रुरुं वने॥६॥
verses.english: While he was thus lamenting in sorrow for the loss of his bride a heaven's messenger came to him in the forest and addressed hiin thus:

verses.sanskrit:
देवदूत उवाच।
              अभिधत्से ह यद्वाचा रुरो दुःखेन तन्मृषा। यतो मर्त्यस्य धर्मात्मन्नायुरस्ति गतायुषः॥७॥
verses.english: The Devaduta said: O Ruru, the words that you are uttering in grief can have no effect; for, O noble-minded (Rishi), one belonging to this world, whose days are run out, cannot come back to life again.

verses.sanskrit: गतायुरेषा कृपणा गन्धर्वाप्सरसोः सुता। तस्माच्छोके मनस्तात मा कृथास्त्वं कथंचन॥८॥
verses.english: This poor child of the Gandharva and the Apsara has her days run out; therefore, O child, do not give yourself up to grief.

verses.sanskrit: उपायश्चात्र विहितः पूर्वं देवैर्महात्मभिः। तं यदीच्छसि कर्तुं त्वं प्राप्स्यसीह प्रमद्वराम्॥९॥
verses.english: The great deities, however, have provided beforehand a means. If you comply with it, you may get back your Pramadvara.

verses.sanskrit:
रुरुरुवाच।
              क उपायः कृतो देवैर्बूहि तत्त्वेन खेचर। करिष्येऽहं तथा श्रुत्वा त्रातुमर्हति मां भवान्॥१०॥
verses.english: Ruru said: O messenger of heaven, (tell me) what means have been provided beforehand by the deities. Tell me in full, so that I may comply with it. You should save me.

verses.sanskrit:
देवेदूत उवाच।
              आयुषोऽर्धं प्रयच्छ त्वं कन्यायै भृगुनन्दन। एवमुत्थास्यति रुरो तव भार्या प्रयद्वरा॥११॥
verses.english: The Devaduta said : O Descendant of Bhrigu, give up half of your own life to your bride and O Ruru, your Pramadvara will then rise from the ground.

verses.sanskrit:
रुरुरुवाच।
              आयुषोऽर्धं प्रयच्छामि कन्यायै खेचरोत्तम। शृङ्गाररूपाभरणा समुत्तिष्ठतु मे प्रिया॥१२॥
verses.english: Ruru said: O best of heaven's messengers, 1 give up half of my life to my bride. Let my beloved one rise in the beautiful form decked with ornaments.

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              ततो गन्धर्वराजश्च देवदूतश्च सत्तमौ। धर्मराजमुपेत्येदं वचनं प्रत्यभाषताम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Sauti said: The king of the Gandharvas and the greatly qualified messenger of heaven, both went to the Deity Dharma and addressed him thus :

verses.sanskrit: धर्मराजायुषोऽर्धेन रुरोर्भार्या प्रमद्वरा। समुत्तिष्ठतु कल्याणी मृतैवं यदि मन्यसे॥१४॥
verses.english: "O king Dharma, if it please you, let the beautiful bride of Ruru, Pramadvara, who is dead, rise up endued with a half of Ruru's life.”

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मराज उवाच।
              प्रमद्वरां रुरोर्भार्यां देवदूत यदीच्छसि। उत्तिष्ठत्वायुषोऽर्धेन रुरोरेव समन्विता॥१५॥
verses.english: The Dharmaraja said : "O messenger of heaven, if it be your wish, let the bride of Ruru Pramadvara, rise up endued with a half of Ruru's life.

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              एवमुक्ते ततः कन्या सोदतिष्ठत्प्रमद्वरा। रुरोस्तस्यायुषोऽर्धेन सुप्तेव वरवर्णिनी॥१६॥
verses.english: Sauti said : When Dharma thus spoke, the beautiful Pramadvara, the betrothed bride of Ruru, rose up as from a slumber, with a half of Ruru's life.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्दृष्टं भविष्ये हि रुरोरुत्तमतेजसः। आयुषोऽतिप्रवृद्धस्य भार्यार्थेऽर्धमलुप्यत॥१७॥
verses.english: It was seen afterwards that the bestowal of a half of his own life to resuscitate his bride by Ruru of long life, led to a curtailment of his own life.

verses.sanskrit: तत इष्टेऽहनि तयोः पितरौ चक्रतुर्मुदा। विवाहं तौ च रेमाते परस्परहितैषिणौ॥१८॥
verses.english: Thereupon their fathers gladly married them off with due rites and the couple passed their days devoted to each other.
verses.bhavadeepa: न चैवमायुषोऽर्धप्रदानेनेतरेषामप्यायुर्लाभो भवतीत्याह । भविष्ये रुरोरेव जातके इदं दृष्टं नान्यत्रेत्यर्थः ॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: स लब्ध्वा दुर्लभां भार्यां पद्मकिञ्जल्कसुप्रभाम्। व्रतं चक्रे विनाशाय जिह्मगानां धृतव्रतः॥१९॥
verses.english: Thus having obtained a wife, difficult to be obtained, who was beautiful and bright as the filaments of the lotus, the Rishi of hard austerities (Ruru) made a vow to destroy the serpent race.

verses.sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा जिह्मगान्सर्वांस्तीव्रकोपसमन्वितः। अभिहन्ति यथा सत्त्वं गृह्य प्रहरणं सदा॥२०॥
verses.english: Whenever he saw a snake, he was filled with great anger and he always killed it with a weapon.
verses.bhavadeepa: एवं कामप्रतीघाते क्रोधावेशादविवेकेनाधर्ममपि महान्तोनुतिष्ठन्तीत्याह । व्रतमिति । व्रतं नियमम् । जिह्मगानां सर्पाणाम् ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: स कदाचिद्वनं विप्रो रुरुरभ्यागमन्महत्। शयानं तत्र चापश्यत् डुण्डुभं वयसान्वितम्॥२१॥
verses.english: One day, the Brahmana, Ruru entered into a very large forest. He saw an old Dundubha snake lying on the ground.

verses.sanskrit: तत उद्यम्य दण्डं स कालदण्डोपमं तदा। जिघांसुः कुपितो विप्रस्तमुवाचाऽथ डुण्डुभः॥२२॥
verses.english: Thereupon with the intention of killing it, Ruru raised his staff in anger, A staff like the staff of Death. The Dundubha then said to the angry Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit: नापराध्यामि ते किंचिदहमद्य तपोधन। संरम्भाच्च किमर्थं मामभिहंसि रुषान्वितः॥२३॥
verses.english: "O Rishi, I have done you no harm. Why should you kill me in anger?"
